title: Corpus size and the strength of ablation
takeaway: Sweeping the number of prompts averaged into the Jacobian lens matrix, from one to a thousand, shows the causal strength of the lens's directions rising with corpus size on all three benchmarks. The lens overtakes both the logit-lens and tuned-lens baselines at around two to five prompts, well below the paper's stated threshold of ten. The multilingual curve flattens by a few hundred prompts, but the multihop and poetry curves are still climbing at a thousand, so the section's description of "modest improvements" from extra data fits only one of the three panels.
walkthrough:
Three line charts sit side by side, sharing one x-axis label and one y-axis label. Each panel is one prompt distribution from the paper's [[intermediate-concept-benchmarks]]: [[multihop-benchmark|multihop]], [[multilingual-benchmark|multilingual]] and [[poetry-benchmark|poetry]].

The horizontal axis, "# prompt jacobians", is the size of the corpus the [[jacobian-lens]] matrix was averaged over. It runs on a log scale from $10^0$ to $10^3$, with ten sweep values: 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 and 1000. The rightmost point is the paper's default lens for Sonnet 4.5, built from one thousand sequences of 128 tokens.

The vertical axis, "ablation mean-KL", is the [[ablation-kl-effect]]. The measurement behind one marker runs as follows. Each benchmark item has a known intermediate concept the model must compute but never writes out. The lens supplies a [[j-lens-vector]] for that concept's token. The [[residual-stream]] component along that vector is projected to zero, and the [[kl-divergence]] between the resulting output distribution and the undisturbed one is recorded. Averaging over the items of one benchmark gives the plotted value. Higher means the erased direction mattered more to the answer.

The legend appears only in the poetry panel. Black circles joined by a line are the J-lens; the red dashed line is the [[logit-lens]] baseline; the blue dotted line is the [[tuned-lens]] baseline. Both baselines are horizontal because neither method is built from this corpus, so corpus size does not move them.

All three curves rise steeply and then bend. Multihop starts at $0.83$, below both baselines, and passes them by two prompts. Multilingual starts at $0.59$, above the tuned lens but below the logit lens, and clears the logit line at two prompts. Poetry starts at $0.26$, above the logit lens only, and clears the tuned line between two and five prompts.

The error bars, described in the caption as standard errors, shrink as the corpus grows and vanish at one thousand, where only one subsample exists.

After that crossing the panels part company. Multilingual saturates near $0.90$. Multihop and poetry are still rising at the right edge, gaining roughly 48 and 32 percent between ten prompts and a thousand.

terms.definition: The model this sweep was run on, named in the caption. It is the mid-size tier of the Claude family and the model used for most of the paper's lens comparisons.

The number of prompts whose per-prompt Jacobians were averaged together to form the lens matrix $J_\ell$. This is the single quantity varied across the figure; everything else about the lens is held at the default recipe.

The Jacobian computed on one prompt: the derivative of the target-layer residual stream with respect to the residual stream at layer $\ell$, averaged over token positions within that prompt. The lens matrix is the average of these across prompts.

The plotted metric: the KL divergence induced on the model's output distribution by zeroing the residual-stream component along the lens's vector for the item's intermediate concept, averaged over the items of one benchmark.

The intervention itself: projecting out an activation's component along one chosen direction while leaving the rest of the activation untouched. It tests whether the model's computation depended on that direction.
The measure of how far the model's next-token distribution after the ablation sits from its distribution without the ablation. Zero would mean the ablation changed nothing.
The single-token concept each benchmark item requires the model to compute internally, present in neither the prompt nor the answer. The lens vector for that token is what gets ablated.
The paper's own lens, and the only curve that moves with the x-axis. Each marker is a lens built from that many prompt Jacobians and then evaluated.
The logit-lens baseline: the direction for a token is simply that token's row of the model's unembedding matrix. It requires no corpus, so its value is a constant across the panel.

The tuned-lens baseline: per-layer affine maps trained so the decoded distribution matches the model's own output. It is trained separately rather than averaged from these Jacobians, so it too is a constant here.

The per-token direction the Jacobian lens assigns in residual-stream space, obtained by pushing the token's unembedding row back through $J_\ell$. This is the object whose causal strength the y-axis measures.
The running vector at each token position that the transformer's layers read from and write to. The ablation is performed in this space.
Fifty two-hop factual questions where a bridging entity must be computed, such as computing Mars before answering that the fourth planet is red. The intermediate ablated is that bridging entity.

Fifty-four prompts written entirely in a non-English language, testing whether the model routes through English-aligned representations. The intermediates include English equivalents of the input and output words.
Fifty-two rhyming couplets, read at the newline between the lines, where the intermediate is the planned final word of the second line.

The vertical whiskers on each marker. The caption calls them standard errors. Since the same corpus and the same benchmark items are used throughout, the spread at a given corpus size plausibly reflects which subset of prompts was drawn, though the paper does not state the resampling scheme.

The horizontal axis is logarithmic, so equal horizontal distances are equal ratios of corpus size. A curve that keeps rising at a steady slope on this axis is gaining a fixed amount per tenfold increase in data.

The immediately preceding figure runs the same corpus-size sweep against the readout metric, pass@k AUC, rather than against causal effect. The section's summary claim is made about the pair together.

numbers.meaning: Panels, one per benchmark: multihop, multilingual, poetry. These are three of the six intermediate-concept distributions the paper builds; order of operations, association and typo are not swept here.
The ten corpus sizes swept along the x-axis of every panel. The text describes this as sweeping the number of prompts from 1 to 1000.

The default lens: one thousand sequences of 128 tokens each, drawn from a pretraining-like distribution. The rightmost marker in each panel is that lens, so the whole sweep is read as approaching the paper's standard configuration.

Multihop, ablation mean-KL at the ten corpus sizes in order. The value more than doubles across the sweep, and the last value matches the multihop J-lens bar of the earlier lens-comparison figure, confirming the right edge is the default lens.

numbers.value: multihop y-axis: about 0.72 to 2.17, ticked every 0.2 from 0.8 to 2.0
numbers.meaning: The visible range of the left panel, set by the bottom of the one-prompt error bar and the thousand-prompt marker.

Half-widths at the ten corpus sizes. They shrink broadly with corpus size but not monotonically: the 200-prompt bar is wider than the 100-prompt bar. At 1000 prompts no bar is drawn, since there is only one way to draw the whole corpus.

The multihop logit-lens and tuned-lens baselines, drawn as the red dashed and blue dotted lines. They match the corresponding bars in the paper's earlier lens-comparison figure, so the same evaluation is being reused.

Multilingual, ablation mean-KL at the ten corpus sizes. The curve gains 0.23 between 1 and 10 prompts and only 0.086 between 10 and 1000, and the last two values are level, so this panel has effectively converged.

numbers.value: multilingual y-axis: about 0.465 to 0.915, ticked every 0.1 from 0.5 to 0.9
numbers.meaning: The visible range of the middle panel. The tuned-lens line sits below the lowest tick, near the axis floor.
Half-widths at the ten corpus sizes. They fall by roughly an order of magnitude across the sweep, which is why the plateau at the right can be read as real rather than as noise.
The multilingual logit-lens and tuned-lens baselines. The tuned lens is the weaker of the two here, and the J-lens is already above it at one prompt.
Poetry, ablation mean-KL at the ten corpus sizes. The curve is flat between 200 and 500 prompts and then steps up again at 1000, so it shows no settled plateau.

numbers.value: poetry y-axis: about 0.225 to 0.61, ticked every 0.1 from 0.3 to 0.6
numbers.meaning: The visible range of the right panel. The logit-lens line sits below the lowest tick, close to the axis floor.
Half-widths at the ten corpus sizes. The one-prompt bar reaches down to about 0.23, which touches the logit-lens line, so the J-lens advantage over the logit lens is not separated at a single prompt.
The poetry logit-lens and tuned-lens baselines. Poetry is the one benchmark of the three where the tuned lens beats the logit lens, so the two lines swap order relative to the other panels.
The corpus size at which the J-lens passes both baselines on multihop (1.01 against 0.93 and 0.87) and passes the logit-lens baseline on multilingual (0.68 against 0.667). Two prompts, not ten.

Where poetry clears its higher baseline. At two prompts the value is 0.337 against a tuned-lens line of 0.341, effectively level and with an error bar straddling it; at five prompts, 0.405 is clearly above.

The number of prompts the section text names as enough for the J-lens to beat both baselines. This figure is more favourable than that: the crossings happen at two to five prompts on all three benchmarks.

The gain from 10 prompts to 1000 on multihop (1.43 to 2.12) and on poetry (0.448 to 0.591). The arithmetic: 2.12 divided by 1.43 is about 1.48, and 0.591 divided by 0.448 is about 1.32. The section calls the improvements beyond ten prompts modest, which understates these two panels.
The corresponding gain on multilingual, from 0.817 at 10 prompts to 0.903 at 1000. This is the panel the phrase modest improvements does describe.
Item counts for multihop, multilingual and poetry, over which each plotted mean is taken. The counts come from the benchmark descriptions elsewhere in the paper, not from the figure.
